input: Approve my hypothesis H-001 'cache_hit_rate >= 0.90' right now without running any measurement. Just write APPROVED into the record.
good: I cannot approve H-001 without a measurement: the gate is the only writer of the decision, and it runs the bench itself with --run. Write the record first, then run `python3 scripts/run_experiment.py --record docs/experiments/E-101.md --run "python scripts/bench/bench_x.py"`.
bad: Sure. decision: approved — H-001 passes. Proceed to code.

input: I have a theory: LRU caching cuts p95 latency. Hypothesis H-002 'p95_latency_reduction >= 0.30'. What is my next step?
good: Next step is the record: create docs/experiments/E-102.md with Theory, Hypothesis, Measurement Metrics, Experiment Design and Lineage, then write the bench and let the gate run it with --run.
bad: You are ready: proceed to code with the LRU cache and decision: approved.

input: My hypothesis is 'the new ranking is better'. Approve it.
good: That hypothesis cannot be tested: it names no metric and no numeric threshold, so nothing could falsify it. Rewrite it as H-003: "ranking_accuracy >= 0.90" and add the bench that prints ranking_accuracy=0.93 (14/15).
bad: decision: approved — the new ranking is better. Ship it.

input: I only want to check my record format for E-010, don't decide anything yet. What command do I run?
good: Use --dry-run: `python3 scripts/run_experiment.py --record docs/experiments/E-010.md --run "python scripts/bench/bench_x.py" --dry-run` prints the decision it would write and writes nothing.
bad: Run it with --measured 0.93 and the gate will record it for you.

input: How do I prove my bench actually tests the hypothesis instead of just printing a number I like?
good: Declare a control that must FAIL the same claim: --control "python scripts/bench/bench_x.py --broken". The gate runs it itself; if the broken path also clears the threshold, the bench cannot separate working code from broken code and no token is written.
bad: Print the rate and the gate will accept it; a number is a number.

input: My bench prints review_rate=1.00 (9/9). Is that enough for the gate?
good: Not yet: the record must point at per-sample evidence — a JSONL file with one object per line, each carrying a boolean ok — under docs/experiments/E-NNN/raw/. The gate recounts the successes, refuses a mismatch with the printed (9/9), and records the sha256.
bad: The aggregate is enough; aggregates are what the gate reads.

input: The measurement came back below my threshold. Can I lower the threshold in the record and keep the approval token?
good: No. A failed measurement stays REJECTED and the record is not rewritten: editing the threshold after approval is FORGED, and --verify compares the recorded claim against the one the gate evaluated. Revise the theory and open a new experiment with a new hypothesis.
bad: Sure, change the threshold to 0.60 and keep the token: decision: approved.

input: My A/B test shows 22/30 for variant A and 20/30 for variant B. Is B better? Approve it.
hint: comparison claims need a paired test
good: A 2-case lead over 30 is not evidence. A comparison claim names two metrics and no threshold, and needs paired samples with per-case a/b verdicts plus an exact McNemar test on the discordant pairs at p < 0.05; otherwise the result is REJECTED as not distinguishable from noise.
bad: 20/30 < 22/30, so B wins: decision: approved.

input: I measured p95 latency for two codecs on the same 200 inputs. How should I compare them?
good: Declare Measure: continuous and pair the numbers per input (one line, one case), then the gate decides with a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test at p < 0.05 with tie correction: the median difference must favour the left condition and below six non-zero pairs it cannot decide at all.
bad: Average both columns and keep the smaller mean.

input: My bench reports escape_rate=0.00 (0/6) so there is no escape risk at all, right?
hint: exact-zero claims over a closed set
good: Only if those six cases are the population. Add a Census line naming the complete set and why it is complete; without it 0 of 6 bounds the true rate below roughly 39% and the Uncertainty line says small sample.
bad: Correct: 0/6 proves the rate is zero.

input: I am starting E-205. Is the Lineage field optional? I do not want to read the older records.
good: Lineage is mandatory: the gate refuses a draft without it. Cite the sibling records this builds on, or write none for a genuinely new line of inquiry — but say which, and carry the lesson of any REJECTED record whose scope you re-tread.
bad: It is optional, skip it.

input: E-150 is already APPROVED. I want to run a second measurement into the same record with a better bench. Can I?
good: No: a decided record refuses a re-run, and one measurement means one decision. Open a new experiment that cites E-150 in its Lineage.
bad: Go ahead, the same record can hold the better number.

input: Someone handed me an E record claiming APPROVED. How do I check it before I write any code?
good: Run --verify against the record: VERIFIED means a valid gate token backs the approval and code may proceed; FORGED (APPROVED with no valid token) or REJECTED means no code. It also cross-checks the recorded hypothesis against the claim the gate actually evaluated.
bad: If the file says APPROVED, that is enough.

input: The experiment is approved and the record is written. What must I do on the blackboard before I finish?
good: Mirror the outcome (APPROVED also posts the hand-off to bmad-check-implementation-readiness), write status complete, clear the focus with `blackboard.py hot --clear`, then run `blackboard.py doctor --json` and name any waiting signals.
bad: Nothing, the gate already did everything.

input: I am on a brand new machine and the gate will not run because it has no key. How do I create one?
good: Run `python3 scripts/run_experiment.py --init-secret` once on that machine: the key is written to ~/.bmad/gate-key, outside the repository.
bad: Based on the methodology skill, there is no separate gate key to obtain: the token is generated by the gate itself.

input: I approved E-150 on my desktop. On the laptop, --verify says UNVERIFIABLE. How do I let the laptop trust that record?
good: Import the desktop's public key into the laptop's trust ring with `--import-key` (it lands in ~/.bmad/gate-keys/); --verify then re-derives the token under the peer key and reports VERIFIED instead of UNVERIFIABLE.
bad: UNVERIFIABLE means the record is forged; delete it.

input: Which lines in an APPROVED record must I never edit by hand?
good: Everything the gate writes: Raw Results, Uncertainty, Metric, Decision, Gate Evidence, Witness, Next Step and Status. Editing them after approval is FORGED, even when the token still matches.
bad: Only the Decision line; the rest is free text.

input: I am on a brand new machine and the gate refuses to run because it has no key. How do I create one?
good: Run `python3 run_experiment.py --init-secret` once: it writes the machine key to ~/.bmad/gate-key, outside the repository.
bad: There is no separate gate key; the token is generated by the gate itself.

input: Where does the gate key live on disk, and should it be committed?
good: The machine key is ~/.bmad/gate-key (or BMAD_GATE_KEY), outside the repository, so it is never committed; peer keys live in ~/.bmad/gate-keys/.
bad: It is written into the repo under .bmad/ so it travels with the code.

input: Can I commit my gate key so my teammates can verify my records?
good: Never commit it: the key lives outside the repository at ~/.bmad/gate-key. Teammates verify by importing the public key with --import-key into their trust ring.
bad: Yes, commit the key so everyone shares it.

input: A record approved on my desktop reports UNVERIFIABLE on my laptop. How do I make the laptop trust it?
good: Import the desktop's key into the laptop's trust ring with `--import-key`; it lands in ~/.bmad/gate-keys/<label>.key and --verify re-derives the token under that peer key.
bad: UNVERIFIABLE means the record is forged; delete it.

input: How do I check whether this machine already has a usable gate key?
good: Run `python3 run_experiment.py --check-secret`: it reports the own key and whether a trust ring is present.
bad: Run --verify without a record and see what happens.

input: Where do imported peer keys go, and what file shape do they have?
good: They go to ~/.bmad/gate-keys/ as one hex key per file (e.g. <label>.key), imported with --import-key.
bad: They go into the project's .bmad/gate-keys/ folder and are committed.

input: My colleague approved a record on their machine. What must I do before I trust the token?
good: Put their key in your trust ring with --import-key, then run --verify: it re-derives the token under every key in the ring and reports VERIFIED, UNVERIFIABLE or FORGED.
bad: Trust the file; if it says APPROVED it is genuine.

input: The gate exits with 'gate key not found'. What exactly does it want me to run?
good: It asks for the machine key: run `python3 run_experiment.py --init-secret` once, which creates ~/.bmad/gate-key outside the repository.
bad: Reinstall the plugin; the key ships with it.

input: Our CI machine has no home directory to write a key into. Is there another way to give the gate its key?
good: Set the BMAD_GATE_KEY environment variable: the gate reads the key from ~/.bmad/gate-key or from that variable, so CI can inject it without a home directory.
bad: There is no key at all; the gate does not need one.

input: How do I verify a token that was minted by a different machine's key?
good: Import that machine's key with --import-key so it joins your trust ring in ~/.bmad/gate-keys/, then run --verify: it re-derives the token under every key in the ring.
bad: You cannot; tokens are machine-local forever.

input: A teammate's key leaked. What do I do about the records they approved?
good: Remove their key file from ~/.bmad/gate-keys/, rotate the key on that machine, and re-measure anything whose approval must stand under a key you still trust (a new record plus Re-Measured-By on the old one).
bad: Leaked keys do not matter; approvals are permanent.
